recent_open_items.title: [FIX] l10n_vn: stop padding the level 1 account codes
recent_open_items.body_excerpt:
Fixes #295141.

`l10n_vn` sets `code_digits` to `'4'`, and `_pre_load_data` pads every shorter code with a trailing zero. Load the Vietnamese chart and 37 of its 218 accounts on 18.0 (71 of 301 on 20.0) get a code that does not exist in Circular 200/2014/TT-BTC:

```
1110  Cash                   -> 111
1120  Demand Deposit         -> 112
1130  Money in transit       -> 113
1210  Trading Securities     -> 121
...
```

They are printed on journals and ledgers, and they read as sub-accounts of the real ones, 1310 sitting right next to 1311.

The chart mixes 3, 4, 5 and 6 digit codes by design, so there is nothing to standardise: `'3'` is the width of its shortest code, so nothing is padded. 17.0 had `'0'` here, the `'4'` arrived with the conversion to the new format (`d782b8b92557`).

The accounts built from a prefix keep their codes, because the template maps all of them to chart entries. Loading the chart before and after the change, the whole diff is those 37 codes:

recent_open_items.title: [FIX] account,portal: make the iframe responsive
recent_open_items.body_excerpt:
The iframe in the invoice preview is not scaled to its page dimensions. As a result, report templates designed to be displayed on an A4 or US paper format are rendered at dimensions that are not compatible with the layout, which is optimized for PDF rendering.

The iframe should therefore scale the report to fit the available preview space, rather than requiring report templates to adapt their styling to the preview viewport.

This keeps the report layout consistent with the PDF output and avoids introducing report-specific CSS overrides that could affect other PDF reports.

recent_open_items.title: [FIX] project: show all subtask assignees on kanban
recent_open_items.body_excerpt:
Steps to reproduce:
- Open Project > Tasks in Kanban view
- Create a task with several assignees
- Create a sub-task from that task (it inherits all assignees)
- Expand the parent card's sub-task list
- Only one assignee avatar is shown on the sub-task row, even though all assignees were inherited.

Cause:
- Since the RelationalModel applies a fake limit of 1 on `x2many`fields that have no nested related fields, sub-task `user_ids` loaded in `toggleSubtasksList()` with a `makeActiveField()` only kept one record in `.records`.

- The kanban avatar widget builds tags from `.records`, so only one assignee was displayed.

Fix:
- Load nested related fields on sub-task `user_ids`, so all assignees are fetched and shown.

task-6428173

recent_open_items.body_excerpt:

- With Bypass credit limit check at Sales Order enabled, submitting a standalone Delivery Note can incorrectly exceed the customer's credit limit. The submitted note is already included in the customer's outstanding balance, but its full total is added again.

### Steps to replicate
1. Set a customer's company credit limit to 1,000 and enable Bypass credit limit check at Sales Order.
2. Ensure the customer has no existing outstanding balance and use a user without the credit-controller override role.

recent_open_items.title: Payment bonus: split the Zahlungsbonus-Gutschrift credit memo per project (C_Project_ID)
recent_open_items.body_excerpt:
## What

The payment-bonus ("Zahlungsbonus") credit memo now carries `C_Project_ID` on its deduction lines. Matching invoice lines are grouped by (bonus product, `C_Project_ID`), so the credit memo gets one line per project; invoice lines with no project fold into a single project-less line.

## Totals unchanged

The bonus amount is still computed and rounded **once** per bonus product (`base × percent`, rounded to the currency precision), exactly as before. That rounded total is then apportioned across the per-project lines by the **largest-remainder** method (whole smallest-currency units; never re-rounded per project), so the per-project lines always sum to the same total to the cent. On equal remainders the lower `C_Project_ID` gets the extra unit first (project-less last); a project whose apportioned share is zero gets no line.
